Community Mental Health Nursing

Community mental health — levels of intervention, outreach, rehabilitation, family burden and stigma reduction.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the scope of community mental health nursing
  • Explain outreach and follow-up programmes
  • Describe psychosocial rehabilitation
  • Reduce stigma and support families

In simple words

Community mental health nursing takes care to people in their own homes and villages, so that illness is found early, treatment continues and the person stays with the family rather than only in a hospital.

Scope of community mental health

  • Promote mental health and prevent relapse
  • Identify early signs and crisis risk
  • Support treatment adherence and follow-up
  • Care for special groups: children, older people, disaster-affected, alcohol users
  • Rehabilitate and integrate into family and work
  • Educate the community and reduce stigma
  • Train and supervise community workers
  • Link to DMHP, NGO and referral services

Community mental health services in India

  • District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) — outpatient and outreach services in each district
  • Mobile mental health teams visit villages
  • Day-care and halfway homes
  • Occupational and sheltered work units
  • NFAP (National Facility for Active Aging Programme) and old-age homes
  • School-based mental health programmes

Family burden and support

  • Family members carry most chronic psychiatric care and often feel exhausted
  • Assess burden, health and support needs at each visit
  • Provide respite, support groups and counselling
  • Address physical care, nutrition and medicines
  • Watch for abuse of the patient or neglect by the family

🔴 Keep the patient in the community wherever possible

Community care maintains dignity, family life and work better than long institutional care. Rehabilitation means restoring the person’s role, not only reducing symptoms.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Community mental health promotes mental health, finds cases early, and supports treatment.
  2. DMHP provides district-level outreach and outpatient services.
  3. Stigma is reduced through education and contact with people who have recovered.
  4. The nurse trains ASHA workers in early recognition.
  5. Rehabilitation aims at social and vocational integration.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Day-care and halfway homes sit between hospital and home.
  2. Sheltered work builds skills and confidence.
  3. Family burden assessment should be part of every visit.
  4. Confidentiality is essential in small communities.
  5. Follow-up reduces default and relapse.

📌 Memory trick

Community mental health = P-I-R-S: Prevention, Identify, Rehabilitate, Support.

60-second revision

  • Community care finds cases early, supports treatment and prevents relapse.
  • DMHP and mobile teams provide outreach.
  • Family support, respite and burden assessment.
  • Rehabilitation: activity, work, integration.
  • Stigma reduction through education and inclusion.

Test yourself

District-level community mental health services are provided through:

Answer: A. The District Mental Health Programme provides outpatient care, outreach and follow-up in the community.

Stigma against mental illness is reduced by:

Answer: B. Education and normalising contact with people who have recovered reduce fear and prejudice.

A halfway home provides:

Answer: B. A halfway home supports the patient in the transition from hospital to independent family life.

Assessing family burden is done to:

Answer: B. Family burden assessment identifies support needs and prevents exhaustion and abandonment of care.

The main community nurse’s role is:

Answer: B. The community nurse finds cases early, supports adherence, prevents relapse and rehabilitates.
